$comment: Four Boeing aircraft spanning gear codes D, 2D and 3D.
Every unit records `mainGearOuterWidth` (authoritative, FAA) and derives the
gear centreline positions from it. See index.json for the full method, and
data/SOURCES.md section 5 for what is and is not verified.
The 747 (2D/2D2) and A380 (2D/3D2) are NOT included. Their wing-plus-body
gear layouts need the longitudinal and transverse offsets of the body gear
relative to the wing gear, and no source consulted in this build constrains
those. A single outer width cannot close a four-bogie layout the way it
closes a two-strut one, so including them would mean inventing geometry

mtow.basis: FAA Aircraft Characteristics Database, MTOW_lb for ICAO type B738.

maxTaxiWeight.basis: Boeing 737 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, D6-58325-7 Rev C (October 2025), section 7.2.1, Maximum Design Taxi Weight for the 737-800.

tirePressure.basis: Boeing 737 ACAP D6-58325-7 Rev C, section 7.2.1, main gear tire pressure for the 737-800.

pressure.basis: Boeing 737 ACAP D6-58325-7 Rev C, section 7.2.1, nose gear tire pressure for the 737-800.

gears.source: Tire size 27x7.75-15, 12PR from Boeing 737 ACAP D6-58325-7 Rev C section 7.2.1. Longitudinal origin: the nose gear defines x = 0. ASSUMED: the nose gear dual spacing of 533 mm (21 in) is not constrained by any source consulted here and is declared in assumedFields.

Longitudinal position = the FAA wheelbase of 51.2 ft (15 606 mm). Transverse position derived from the FAA main gear outer width of 23.0 ft (7010 mm), which the FAA data dictionary defines as the distance between outer tires: track = 7010 - 864 - 419.1 = 5727 mm, so the strut centreline sits at 2863 mm. That derived track agrees with Boeing's separately published 737 tread of 18 ft 9 in (5715 mm) to within 12 mm, which is the cross-check that supports the 864 mm (34 in) dual spacing. Tire H44.5x16.5-21, 28PR from Boeing 737 ACAP section 7.2.1.
Mirror of MLG-L about the aircraft centreline; same derivation.

units.notes: The most common narrowbody in the world traffic mix and the usual reference case for a D gear.

Longitudinal position = the FAA wheelbase of 60.0 ft (18 288 mm), measured to the main gear centroid, so the tandem spread does not shift it. Transverse position derived from the FAA main gear outer width of 28.0 ft (8534 mm): track = 8534 - 864 - 368.3 = 7302 mm, strut centreline at 3651 mm. That agrees with Boeing's published 757 tread of 24 ft (7315 mm) to within 13 mm. Tire H40x14.5-19 from Boeing 757 ACAP section 7.2. ASSUMED: tandem spacing 1143 mm (45 in) — no source consulted constrains it, and the wheelbase is measured to the centroid so nothing else pins it down. Declared in assumedFields.
